title: Tax Return in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Filing is voluntary for most employees.** With one job, tax class I and no benefits over €410, you only may file. Voluntary returns reach back **four years**, so **2022 closes on 31 December 2026**.

**Some people have to file.** Tax class III/V couples, two jobs at once, more than **€410** of Elterngeld, Kurzarbeitergeld or other untaxed income. For them the **2025 return was due on 31 July 2026**.
**Berlin commutes are short.** At **30 cents** per km for the first 20 km, a 9 km commute on 200 days is only **€540**, less than half the **€1,230** flat allowance your employer already gave you.
**What pushes you over:** your own ticket if it cost more than the allowance, **€6 per home office day** from 2023 (€5 in 2022), work equipment such as a laptop, and union dues.
**Berlin processes fast.** Average **46.3 days** in 2025, the quickest state. The Finanzamt Berlin International, for people living abroad, averaged **90.4 days**.
**My move:** run your numbers in the tool, then file 2022 first and the other open years in the same sitting.
